slot.brief: Give ΔH (or ΔU) for a reaction involving gaseous species and ask for ΔU (or ΔH) using ΔH = ΔU + Δng RT; one-step computation with R = 8.314.

stem:
For the reaction:
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_4(g) + 3\text{O}_2(g) \longrightarrow 2\text{CO}_2(g) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$$
the enthalpy change $\Delta H$ is $-1411.0\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ at $300\ \text{K}$. The change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) for the reaction at the same temperature is:
(Take $R = 8.314\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$)
working:
The relationship between enthalpy change and internal energy change is:
$$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT \implies \Delta U = \Delta H - \Delta n_g RT$$

1. Determine $\Delta n_g$ (change in moles of gaseous species only, excluding liquid $\text{H}_2\text{O}$):
$$\Delta n_g = n_g(\text{products}) - n_g(\text{reactants}) = 2 - (1 + 3) = 2 - 4 = -2\ \text{mol}$$

2. Compute $\Delta n_g RT$:
$$\Delta n_g RT = (-2\ \text{mol}) \times (8.314\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}) \times (300\ \text{K}) = -4988.4\ \text{J mol}^{-1} = -4.9884\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$$

3. Calculate $\Delta U$:
$$\Delta U = -1411.0\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1} - (-4.9884\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}) = -1411.0 + 4.9884 = -1406.01\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1} \approx -1406.0\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Independent check: Δn(gas) = 2 − (1+3) = −2 (H2O is liquid). ΔU = ΔH − ΔnRT = −1411.0 − (−2)(8.314×10⁻³ kJ)(300) = −1411.0 + 4.99 ≈ −1406.0 kJ/mol.

draft.distractor_notes:
A: Sign error in rearranging the thermodynamic relation, computing $\Delta U = \Delta H + \Delta n_g RT = -1411.0 - 4.99 = -1416.0\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.
B: Phase oversight, counting $\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$ as a gas to get $\Delta n_g = 4 - 4 = 0$ and concluding $\Delta U = \Delta H = -1411.0\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.
C: Stoichiometry slip, omitting the coefficient of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4(g)$ to get $\Delta n_g = 2 - 3 = -1$, yielding $\Delta U = -1411.0 - (-2.49) = -1408.5\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.
